experience.title: Researcher, DTec: Law and Technology Group
experience.organisation: Federal University of Minas Gerais, Brazil
details: Conducted comparative legal research on AI discrimination, automated decision-making, biometric data governance, and mitigation strategies across EU, UK, US, and Latin American frameworks.
Examined gaps in AI governance, focusing on fundamental rights, due process, accountability, and public-sector uses of technology.
Co-authored research on algorithmic bias, automated facial recognition, and biometric data management for the Brazilian Centre of Law, Technology and Innovation’s blog.

experience.title: Legal Consultant, Innovation Centre (UAILab)
experience.organisation: State Court of Justice of Minas Gerais (TJMG), Brazil
details: Conducted legal research and prepared opinions on the use of new technologies in court procedures, including compliance with resolutions of Brazil’s National Justice Council (CNJ).

Contributed to CONECTA TJMG, a project to digitalise a Court of Appeal’s caseflow and improve document access and internal procedures for judges and court staff. The initiative was included in CNJ’s national repository of good practices.

Worked with the Court’s Technology Centre and Data Protection Officer to make its internal data protection policy more accessible through legal design and plain language. This initiative was also included in CNJ’s repository.
Collaborated with judicial innovation centres across Brazil through FONÁGIL, supporting judges in developing five prototypes for Special Courts, including one selected for pilot implementation.
Facilitated design thinking workshops with magistrates, judges, court clerks, and administrative staff to improve judicial services, workflows, and access to justice.

education.title: PhD in Law
details: Research within a European Research Council-funded programme (JUDGEASSIST) examining the design, evaluation, and deployment of AI systems that assist judicial decision-making, with a focus on judicial integrity, legitimacy, and European rule of law values.

details: The clinics are intensive, interdisciplinary, semester-long courses, established to teach future leaders in the AI policy field skills in policy analysis, research, evaluation, team management, and policy formation. Topics covered include AI History, AI Issues and Institutions, AI Regulation and Policy Frameworks, and Research Methods.
